name: Per-User Caring History Doctrine
purpose: Define how K-KUT may remember user-specific emotional/sensory history in a personally caring, non-creepy, non-manipulative way.
core_law: Remember to care better. Never remember to manipulate.
allowed_memory: avoidance notes supplied by the buyer
forbidden_memory: inferred trauma without explicit user statement
private facts not needed for HUG delivery
consent_laws: The user must be able to review stored history.
The user must be able to correct stored history.
The user must be able to delete stored history.
Sensitive emotional notes must never be required for purchase.
Do not surprise the user with remembered details in buyer-facing copy.
tone_laws: Never say the system knows the receiver.
Never imply a prior emotional choice defines the user permanently.
Treat change over time as normal.

history_record_shape.buyer_user_id: internal user id or anonymous session id
history_record_shape.relationship_lane: partner | parent | child | friend | mentor | self | family | other
history_record_shape.occasion_or_situation: anniversary | apology | birthday | thank_you | grief_held | encouragement | other
worked_well_notes: what the buyer approved or repeated
avoid_next_time: sounds, words, moods, or lanes to avoid
history_record_shape.human_review_notes: why this history is safe to reuse

use_cases: Suggest a warmer option after a buyer repeatedly chooses gentle care.
Avoid energetic/spark options when the user has marked them as too intense.
Remember that apology routes should stay soft and non-coercive for this buyer.
Keep anniversary suggestions in still-choosing/devotion territory when previously approved.
Hold grief-related history for human review instead of automatic reuse.

safe: Based on what you chose before, here are softer options.
You can change the feeling anytime.
Nothing is assumed about the receiver.
forbidden: This will make them forgive you.
They always respond to this feeling.
Your profile says this is perfect.
